title: Space Tech Briefing — September 30, 2026
summary:
Good morning, space enthusiasts and future voyagers! This is your daily dose of the cosmos, live from Space Technology Radio, and I am thrilled to be your guide through the latest in aerospace. It is **September 30, 2026**, and what an incredible week it has been for space exploration! Let's dive right into the headlines that have been electrifying our orbit.

First up, as we look back at a truly monumental week in space, let's recap a major development from just two days ago, Monday, September 28th. SpaceX's Starship achieved orbital flight for the very first time! This fourteenth flight saw the mighty Super Heavy Block 3, Booster 21, propel Starship Ship 41, the V3 version, into the heavens. The mission's primary objective was to place Starship into a low Earth orbit, approximately 275 kilometers high, for about six revolutions over roughly ten hours. It was a full test of the flight sequence: stage separation, a controlled return and splashdown of the booster in the Gulf of Mexico, followed by the Ship's deorbit, atmospheric re-entry, and an impressive splashdown in the Pacific, west of Chile. While there were no plans to recover the two stages with the launch tower on this historic occasion, the successful orbital flight marks an absolutely colossal step forward for humanity's multi-planetary ambitions!

And while we're reflecting on recent achievements, let's also turn our attention to a critical maneuver by one of Europe's most ambitious missions. The CNES announced that earlier this week, also on September 28th, the JUICE probe made another close pass by Earth. This wasn't just a flyby; it was a crucial gravitational assist, a cosmic slingshot, using our planet's pull to precisely refine its trajectory. This maneuver is vital for JUICE to reach its ultimate destination, the Jovian system, safely in 2031. And even better news for science fans: the probe's instruments were activated during this close approach, gathering valuable data even as it continues its epic journey to Jupiter. What an incredible way to leverage our home planet's gravity for deep space exploration!

And that's our briefing for this dynamic Wednesday morning, September 30, 2026. From groundbreaking orbital flights to crucial interplanetary slingshots, the universe continues to call, and we are answering! Thank you for tuning in to Space Technology Radio. Stay curious, keep looking up, and have a fantastic day!
